questions.question: Where and when did hip-hop originate?
options: In African American and Latino communities in the South Bronx, New York, in the 1970s
questions.explanation: Hip-hop emerged in the South Bronx in the 1970s and has become the world's most commercially dominant musical genre.

questions.question: What is cultural globalization?
options: The transmission of ideas, meanings, and values across national borders, creating shared cultural experiences
questions.explanation: Cultural globalization spreads ideas and values across borders - and English-language music has been one of its most effective channels.

questions.question: How has hip-hop's global spread affected local music cultures?
options: Artists worldwide have adapted hip-hop into local languages and styles, creating hybrid forms
All hip-hop is still performed only in English
Hip-hop is banned outside the USA
questions.explanation: From French rap to Korean hip-hop, artists blend the genre with local languages and traditions - an example of cultural hybridization.

questions.question: Why do many non-English-speaking artists strategically include English in their songs?
options: English phrases increase international appeal and chart potential
It is required by copyright law
questions.explanation: Artists like K-pop groups mix English hooks into their lyrics to reach global audiences while keeping their own language and identity.

questions.question: What tension does the globalization of English-language music create?
options: Between shared global culture and the preservation of local languages and traditions
Between young and old musicians only
questions.explanation: Global English-language pop creates shared experiences but can crowd out local music and languages - the central tension of cultural globalization.
